content:
I've now tried dozens of input names across every plausible category and ALL fail with "unknown-input". This is a strong signal that the input vocabulary is something I'm fundamentally not guessing — possibly a very specific set like single uppercase letters, or the game uses a completely different scheme.

Let me reconsider the whole situation strategically. The goal is farming (till/plant/water parsnips). But maybe I'm overcomplicating. Let me re-read the primitive: `interact {x,y,button,slot?}` — "walks next to the tile, faces it, presses the button". 

What if `button` is meant to be a **number** but the small brain skips falsy AND the earlier numeric 1/2 were skipped because... actually they were skipped too. Hmm, but maybe numeric buttons ARE valid and just weren't logged as failures because they succeeded silently but did nothing visible on the notice board (which "blocks" — maybe you can't interact with it that way).

Wait — that's a real possibility I dismissed! Numeric buttons 1 and 2 produced NO error and NO "fail" line — they were just... not in the failure list. Let me check: in the button:1/2 plan, status showed only "walk_to ok | wait ok" — the interacts weren't mentioned at all. That could mean they were **skipped** OR **succeeded silently**. 

The cleanest test: use numeric button on a SOIL tile with the hoe and then OBSERVE whether the tile becomes tilled. If numeric buttons work, tilling will show. Let me do that and observe carefully.

args.approach: Numeric buttons 1/2 produced no error and no fail line (unlike strings) — they may succeed silently. Test button:1 with hoe on soil tiles, then observe whether tiles become tilled. If yes, numeric buttons are the answer.
